messages.subject: Unexpected behavior multigroup
parts:
Students of mine produced this behavior in working their final exam. The unexpected behavior involves equality constraints across groups in a multigroup analysis. Here is sessionInfo():

 > sessionInfo()
R version 3.3.1 (2016-06-21)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows >= 8 x64 (build 9200)

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252 
[2] LC_CTYPE=English_United States.1252   
[3] LC_MONETARY=English_United States.1252
[4] LC_NUMERIC=C                          
[5] LC_TIME=English_United States.1252    

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods  
[7] base     

other attached packages:
[1] psych_1.6.6     semTools_0.4-13 lavaan_0.5-21  

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] MASS_7.3-45    parallel_3.3.1 tools_3.3.1    mnormt_1.5-4  
[5] pbivnorm_0.6.0 stats4_3.3.1   quadprog_1.5-5

Data file is attached. It includes 1300 observations on 11 variables, 10 indicators plus a grouping variable that defines 3 groups. The fabricated data includes " missing" observations coded as 99, so the first step is to recode all missings as NA:

> data<-read.clipboard()
> data[data==99]<-NA

Here is some model syntax:

model<-'# Factor - Factor - mediator
F4 ~ a * F2 + b * F3
F2 ~ c * F1
F3 ~ d * F1 

#indirect effect
F124 := a*c
F134 := b*d

#strength of path F1-2-3 over F1-3-4
pathdifference := a*c - b*d 

# Factor - Indicator
F4 =~ y8 + y9 + y10
F3 =~ y6 + y7
F2 =~ y4 + y5
F1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3'

'# Factor - Factor
F4 ~ a * F2 + b * F3
F2 ~ c * F1
F3 ~ d * F1 

#indirect effect
F124 := a*c
F134 := b*d

#strength of path F1-2-3 over F1-3-4
pathdifference := a*c - b*d 

# Factor - Indicator
F4 =~ y8 + y9 + y10
F3 =~ y6 + y7
F2 =~ y4 + y5
F1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3'

So the model has 4 factors, with two indirect paths from F1 to F4, by way of F2 and F3. The labels assigned to the structural paths were part of this student's attempt to answer a part of the exam question. Notice that the student applies a single label to each structural coefficient, not a vector of labels.

The strange behavior happens in the comparison of two analyses, one using just the syntax shown, and one using an additional group.equal constraint. Here is the first:

> model1.out <- sem(model=model,data=data, group="group", missing="FIML")
> show(model1.out)
lavaan (0.5-21) converged normally after  65 iterations

  Number of observations per group         
  1                                                300
  2                                                400
  3                                                600

  Number of missing patterns per group     
  1                                                 55
  2                                                 77
  3                                                 99

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic               84.680
  Degrees of freedom                                93
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.719

Notice that DF = 93. There are 3 groups, and with no across-group constraints, this means DF = 31 per group, which is what I expect from the model.

Now the second analysis imposes equality of loadings across groups.  In the model, there are 6 free loadings (the other 4 are fixed to 1 for scaling). If loadings are held equal across he 3 groups, then we will go from 3 groups of 6 estimated loadings to 1 group of 6 estimated loadings, so we will gain 12 DF. But that is not what happens:

> model2.out <- sem(model=model,data=data, group="group", missing="FIML",group.equal=c("loadings"))
> show(model2.out)
lavaan (0.5-21) converged normally after  49 iterations

  Number of observations per group         
  1                                                300
  2                                                400
  3                                                600

  Number of missing patterns per group     
  1                                                 55
  2                                                 77
  3                                                 99

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              146.178
  Degrees of freedom                               113
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.019

DF = 113 now, so the model gained 20 DF, not 12. The extra 8, it turns out, come from the labeled structural paths. In the first analysis, those 4 structural parameters are estimated separately for each of the 3 groups, but in the second analysis, they are constrained equal across groups.

The same thing happens if I use the measurementInvariance function in semTools:

> measurementInvariance(model=model,data=data,group="group",missing="FIML")

Measurement invariance models:

Model 1 : fit.configural
Model 2 : fit.loadings
Model 3 : fit.intercepts
Model 4 : fit.means

Chi Square Difference Test

                Df   AIC   BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff
fit.configural  93 30274 30801  84.68                   
fit.loadings   113 30296 30720 146.18     61.498      20
fit.intercepts 125 30282 30644 156.84     10.659      12

The fit.loadings result constrains *both* loadings and structural paths.

I did not expect this behavior regarding the structural paths to change depending on whether or not loadings are constrained. Is this another case where I just haven't read the documentation closely enough?

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected behavior multigroup
parts:
Ed,
I think that this is related to a similar question that came up earlier this term.

The lavaanify function implements equality constraints by assigning the same parameter label.  As a result, any time that a user includes both the group.equal parameter and user defined parameter labels there is a potential for these to interact.  The lavaanify() function needs to reconcile requests regarding labels made directly in the model specification with those made indirectly through group.equal.  All the groups are combined in one parameter table, and labels are shared within that table.  In other words, you cannot recycle the same label to refer to corresponding parameters in different groups without equating them across groups.

Here is a simplified example:

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
              visual ~ a*textual + b*speed '

lavaanify(HS.model, auto.var=TRUE, auto.fix.first=TRUE,
          auto.cov.lv.x=TRUE, ngroups=2)

If you inspect the parameter table, you see that providing only one label results in applying those labels to only the first group (a and b).  However, combining the same specification with group.equal causes the labels to be applied in every group.

lavaanify(HS.model, auto.var=TRUE, auto.fix.first=TRUE,
          auto.cov.lv.x=TRUE, ngroups=2, group.equal=c("loadings"))

If you change the specification to a vector of a label and an NA, you still get the same behavior with group.equal.

HS.model2 <- 'visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
              visual ~ c(a,NA)*textual + c(b,NA)*speed '

lavaanify(HS.model2, auto.var=TRUE, auto.fix.first=TRUE,
          auto.cov.lv.x=TRUE, ngroups=2, group.equal=c("loadings"))

So, one option would be to avoid using the group.equal parameter in this case and specify the constraints manually.  In this case, the labels for the structural effects are again applied only to the first group.

HS.model3 <- ' visual  =~ c(l1,l1)*x1 + c(l2,l2)*x2 + c(l3,l3)*x3
              textual =~ c(l4,l4)*x4 + c(l5,l5)*x5 + c(l6,l6)*x6
              speed   =~ c(l7,l7)*x7 + c(l8,l8)*x8 + c(l9,l9)*x9
              visual ~ a*textual + b*speed '

lavaanify(HS.model3, auto.var=TRUE, auto.fix.first=TRUE,
          auto.cov.lv.x=TRUE, ngroups=2)

Another option would be to retain group.equal but to explicitly apply different labels in each group.  This means that you need to duplicate the model specification for your computed parameters (not included in my example) if you want them computed separately for each group.

HS.model4 <- 'visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
              visual ~ c(a,c)*textual + c(b,d)*speed '

lavaanify(HS.model4, auto.var=TRUE, auto.fix.first=TRUE,
          auto.cov.lv.x=TRUE, ngroups=2, group.equal=c("loadings"))

Keith

Keith--
     Yes, that seems to be what is happening. The best solution is probably just to ensure that students specify their syntax fully, using the c(...) structure for labels when conducting multiple group analysis. Still, it seems undesirable that syntax behaves differently due to a seemingly unrelated option, all the more so when invoking the measurementInvariance function from semTools.
     Thanks!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected behavior multigroup
parts:
> I did not expect this behavior regarding the structural paths to change
> depending on whether or not loadings are constrained. Is this another
> case where I just haven't read the documentation closely enough?

I understand this may seem 'odd' indeed. The underlying problem is the
following: in the case of multiple groups, users should always use a
*vector* of labels. lavaan will not enforce it, but it is good practice
nonetheless.

lavaan is a bit like the perl language: it allows for multiple ways to
accomplish the same thing, and it is very permissive in the way users
use (and misuse) the model syntax. The labeling system is the
fundamental approach to control equality constraints at the parameter
level. The group.equal= argument is a convenient shortcut with default
choices. Combining labels and the group.equal= argument is tricky.

Yves.
